questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights has been deleted from the original list of fundamental rights provided in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to property**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** property right was originally included in the Constitution of India** as a fundamental right.
 
• However, it was** removed from the list of fundamental rights through the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.**
 
• It was subsequently made a **legal right under Article 300A of the Constitution.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** 

 
• Cultural and educational rights:
 
 
• These rights are still part of the fundamental rights in India.
 
• They are enshrined in Articles 29 and 30 of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• Right to constitutional remedies:
 
 
• This right is also still a fundamental right in India.
 
• It is guaranteed by Article 32 of the Constitution, which allows individuals to directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• Right to freedom of religion:
 
 
• This right is another fundamental right in India.
 
• It is protected by Article 25 to 28 of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which Excel feature allows you to simultaneously edit the same cell or range of cells with multiple users in real-time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**co-authoring**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Co-authoring** in Excel enables multiple users to work on the same spreadsheet simultaneously,

 
 
• making real-time edits and seeing each other's changes as they happen.
 
• This feature is particularly useful for collaborative projects where multiple individuals need to work on the same data.
 
 
 
• For example, a team of accountants might use co-authoring to collaborate on a financial report, while a group of students could use it to work on a group project.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Data Validation:**

 
 
• This feature is used to restrict the type of data that can be entered into a cell or range of cells.
 
 
 
• **Conditional Formatting:**
 
 
• This feature allows you to apply different formatting to cells based on specific conditions.
 
 
 
• **Track Changes:**
 
 
• This feature allows you to track the changes made to a document, including who made the changes and when.

questions.question: A flat ring of small, icy bodies that revolve around the sun beyond the orbit of the planet Neptune is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuiper Belt**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kuiper Belt is a vast region of icy bodies **that extends beyond the orbit of Neptune.
 
• It is** home to many dwarf planets, including Pluto.**
 
• The Oort Cloud is another region of icy bodies,
 
• It is located even farther from the sun than the Kuiper Belt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bow Shock**

 
 
• A bow shock is a region of turbulent plasma that forms when a high-speed plasma flow encounters a stationary obstacle.
 
• While there are bow shocks in space, particularly around planets with magnetic fields, they do not refer to a flat ring of icy bodies.
 
 
 
• ** Oort Cloud**
 
 
• The Oort Cloud is a spherical region of icy bodies that extends far beyond the Kuiper Belt.
 
• While both the Kuiper Belt and Oort Cloud contain icy bodies, the Oort Cloud is not a flat ring and is located at a much greater distance from the Sun.
 
 
 
• **Asteroid Belt**
 
 
• The Asteroid Belt is a region of rocky bodies located between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
 
• While both the Asteroid Belt and Kuiper Belt contain celestial bodies, the Asteroid Belt is primarily composed of rocky asteroids, not icy bodies, and is located closer to the Sun.

questions.question: In Cricket, the bowler does NOT get credit for _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** to run out**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **If the batter is run out**, the run does not count and the bowler does not get credit for the wicket.
 
• A run out can happen when: 
 
 
• A fielder throws the ball at the wicket 
 
• A batter leaves the crease when the ball is not dead 
 
• So the run-out get credit in cricket
 
 
 
• Run out
 
 
• A run-out occurs when the batter is dismissed by being hit the wicket with the ball before they can ground their bat or any part of their body.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** LBW**

 
 
• LBW (Leg Before Wicket) occurs when the ball pitches in front of the wicket, strikes the batter's leg, and would have gone on to hit the wicket had it not been stopped by the batter's leg.
 
 
 
• ** Bowled**
 
 
• Bowled occurs when the batter is dismissed by having the ball hit their wicket directly.
 
 
 
• ** Catch**
 
 
• A catch occurs when the fielder catches the ball before it touches the ground.

questions.question: The approach driven by seven engines, which is powered by Clean Energy and ‘Sabka Prayas’ is related to which scheme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PM Gati Shakti's Master Plan**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• A revolutionary strategy for sustainable development and economic prosperity is PM GatiShakti. Seven engines—roads, railways, airports, ports, mass transit, waterways, and logistics infrastructure—power the strategy.
 
• The Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman, stated that the seven engines will work together to propel the economy ahead while presenting the Union Budget 2022–23 to Parliament today.
 
• The complementing responsibilities of energy transmission, IT communication, bulk water & sewerage, and social infrastructure support these engines.
 
• In the end, she claimed, the strategy is driven by clean energy and Sabka Prayas, the combined efforts of the federal government, state governments, and the private sector, which will provide a tonne of job and business opportunities for everyone, especially the young.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan**

 
 
• It is Launched in June 2020, the Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan aims to provide employment opportunities to migrant workers who lost their jobs during the COVID-19 pandemic and returned to their home states.
 
• The scheme focuses on creating durable assets and infrastructure in rural areas through various projects related to roads, housing, irrigation, and sanitation, thereby enhancing rural livelihoods.
 
• The initiative has a budget of approximately Rs. 50,000 crore and targets 125 days of guaranteed wage employment for each worker.
 
• It encompasses multiple states and involves local self-governments and various ministries.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana**
 
 
• It is Launched in April 2015, this scheme aims to provide financial support to small and micro enterprises by offering loans up to Rs. 10 lakh without requiring collateral, promoting entrepreneurship among the lower-income segments of society.
 
• The Mudra Yojana categorizes loans into three types: Shishu (up to Rs. 50,000), Kishore (Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5 lakh), and Tarun (Rs. 5 lakh to Rs. 10 lakh), catering to the varying needs of entrepreneurs at different stages.
 
• The scheme has facilitated millions of loans to small businesses across India, boosting self-employment and job creation while contributing to the overall economic growth of the country.
 
 
 
• **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana**
 
 
• It is Launched in October 2020 as part of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Package, this scheme aims to incentivize employers to create new jobs and restore jobs lost during the COVID-19 pandemic by providing financial support.
 
• Under this scheme, the government provides a subsidy to employers for the new jobs created.
 
• It covers a significant portion of the employee's provident fund contributions for a specified period, reducing the financial burden on employers.
 
• The Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana targets various sectors, focusing on encouraging the employment of women and marginalized communities, thereby promoting inclusive growth and sustainable employment opportunities.​

questions.question: Who was the first Indian wrestler to win a world championship medal?

• His achievement not only brought pride to India but also paved the way for future generations of Indian wrestlers.

• KD Jadhav is renowned for his bronze medal win in the 62 kg freestyle wrestling category at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics.
 
• This achievement brought India its first individual Olympic medal in wrestling.
 
• He was a multiple-time national champion in India, showcasing his dominance in the sport.
 
 
 
• Dara Singh:
 
 
• Dara Singh was a prominent figure in both the world of wrestling and Bollywood.
 
• He won numerous wrestling titles and starred in numerous popular films.
 
• His popularity helped to popularize wrestling in India, making it a widely recognized sport.
 
 
 
• Malwa Singh:

questions.question:
Calculate personal income (in Rs. crore) from the given data. 

 
 

 **Particulars **
 Rs. (in crore)&l
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1050**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Calculating Personal Income
 
 
• Private Income:
 
 
• This is the total income earned by individuals and businesses within a country, excluding government income.
 
 
 
• Net Retained Earnings:
 
 
• These are the profits that a company keeps after paying dividends to shareholders.
 
 
 
• Corporation Tax:
 
 
• This is a tax levied on the profits of corporations.
 
 
 
 
 
• Formula Used :
 
 
• Personal Income = Private Income - Net Retained Earnings - Corporation Tax
 
 
 
• **Given Data:**
 
 
• Private Income = Rs. 1800 crore
 
• Net Retained Earnings = Rs. 500 crore
 
• Corporation Tax = Rs. 250 crore
 
 
 
• Personal Income = 1800 crore - 500 crore - 250 crore = 1050 crore
 
• **Therefore, the personal income is Rs. 1050 crore.**

questions.question: Which of the following food grains highly benefited from the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wheat**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Green Revolution increased the yields of** wheat and rice, **the most benefited food grains.
 
• The green revolution was a period of agricultural innovation that took place in the 1960s and 1970s.
 
• Its aim was to increase the productivity of crops and ensure food security for the growing population.
 
• Food grains were the main beneficiaries of the green revolution.
 
• Crops like wheat and rice were developed to be high-yielding and disease-resistant
 
• This led to a reduction in food shortages and a decrease in prices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Vegetables, oilseeds, and pulses also benefited from the green revolution, but to a lesser extent. 
 
• Oilseeds refer to crops like soybean, cottonseed, and sunflower that are grown for their oil content.
 
 
• The green revolution led to the development of high-yielding varieties of these crops, which helped to meet the growing demand for cooking oil.
 
 
 
• Pulses are a group of crops that includes lentils, chickpeas, and beans.
 
 
• These crops are a good source of protein, but their productivity was low before the green revolution.
 
• New varieties of pulses were developed that were more productive and had better resistance to pests and diseases.

questions.question: Article 15 of the Constitution of India entails:

options.text: prohibition of discrimination against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 15 of the Constitution of India prohibits discrimination by the state against any citizen on these specific grounds.**
 
• It ensures equality and protects individuals from being discriminated against in matters such as access to public places, use of public facilities, and other civil rights.
 
• Article 15 ensures that no citizen is discriminated against by the state based on religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth in various spheres of life, including access to public facilities and services.
 
• It also empowers the state to make special provisions for women, children, and socially and educationally backward classes, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Freedom of speech and expression (Article 19)**:

 
 
• Article 19(1)(a) guarantees all citizens the right to freely express their thoughts, opinions, and beliefs without fear of censorship or punishment.
 
• However, this right is subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of sovereignty, public order, decency, or security of the state. 
 
 
 
• **Cultural and educational rights (Articles 29 and 30)**:
 
 
• Article 29 ensures that any section of citizens with a distinct language, script, or culture has the right to conserve it, and it also prohibits denial of admission to educational institutions based on these grounds.
 
• Article 30 gives minorities the right to establish and administer their own educational institutions to preserve their cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Equality of opportunity in employment (Article 16)**:
 
 
• Article 16 guarantees equal opportunity for all citizens in matters of public employment or appointment to any office under the state, regardless of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, or place of birth.
 
• The article also allows for reservations or affirmative actions in favor of socially and educationally backward classes to ensure fair representation in public employment.

questions.question: Which of the following is a food-borne disease caused by the consumption of contaminated food or beverages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cholera**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Cholera is a food-borne disease caused by consuming water or food contaminated **with the bacterium Vibrio cholerae.
 
• It** leads to severe diarrhoea and dehydration.**
 
• **The disease is commonly spread in areas with poor sanitation** and unsafe water supplies
 
• he hallmark symptoms of cholera include profuse watery diarrhoea, often described as "rice water stools," vomiting, and severe dehydration.
 
• If left untreated, dehydration can lead to shock, kidney failure, and death, sometimes within hours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tuberculosis** is an infectious disease caused by *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*.

 
 
• It primarily affects the lungs but can spread to other parts of the body.
 
• The disease is transmitted through airborne particles when an infected person coughs or sneezes.
 
 
 
• **Chicken pox** is a highly contagious viral infection caused by the varicella-zoster virus. It causes an itchy rash with red spots and blisters.
 
 
• The disease spreads through direct contact with an infected person or through the air by respiratory droplets.
 
 
 
• **Malaria** is a parasitic disease caused by *Plasmodium* species, transmitted through the bite of an infected Anopheles mosquito.
 
 
• It affects red blood cells and causes symptoms like fever, chills, and anemia, predominantly in tropical and subtropical regions.

questions.question: What was the name of the campaign led by the Ali brothers and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad to save the Ottoman Caliphate as a symbol of unity among the Muslim community?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Khilafat Movement**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Khilafat Movement was led by the Ali brothers (Shaukat Ali and Mohammad Ali) and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**

 
 
• to protest against the disintegration of the Ottoman Empire after World War I and to protect the institution of the Caliphate,
 
 
• which they considered a symbol of unity among Muslims.
 
 
 
• It was a **significant movement in India,** seeking to rally Muslims and Hindus in opposition to British rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Wahabi Movement:
 
 
• It emerged in the early 19th century in India, inspired by the teachings of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab in Arabia.
 
• The movement aimed to purify Islam by removing practices considered to be innovations (bid'ah) and restoring monotheism (tawhid).
 
• It also opposed British colonial rule and encouraged jihad against foreign powers, becoming associated with resistance movements in India.
 
 
 
• Faraizi Movement:
 
 
• It was started by Haji Shariatullah in Bengal in the early 19th century, focusing on the strict observance of Islamic obligations (Faraiz).
 
• The movement sought to eliminate un-Islamic practices and customs that had crept into the lives of Bengali Muslims, particularly under British rule.
 
• It also had an anti-landlord and anti-colonial component, with a significant following among peasants, advocating for their rights against oppressive landlords.
 
 
 
• Ahmadiya Movement:
 
 
• Founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in 1889 in India, the movement claims that Ahmad is the promised Messiah and Mahdi of Islam.
 
• It promotes peaceful propagation of Islam and stresses rational discourse, interfaith harmony, and religious tolerance.
 
• The movement is controversial within mainstream Islam due to its belief in Ahmad’s prophetic role, which is seen by some as a challenge to the finality of Prophet Muhammad’s prophethood

questions.question: Which of the following airports is being built as India’s first ‘carbon-neutral airport’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leh airport**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Leh Airport is being built as India's first **carbon-neutral airport**. 
 
• The airport will use a geothermal system and solar PV plant to **heat and cool the terminal building.** 
 
• The system will concentrate naturally existing heat and use it for space heating, cooling, and water heating.

questions.question: Who among the following confirmed Maxwell's theories with the discovery of radio waves and also became the first person to transmit and receive controlled radio waves in 1886?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heinrich Hertz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Heinrich Hertz**

 
 
• Scottish physicist James Clerk Maxwell, who developed a unified theory of electromagnetism in the 1870s, predicted the existence of radio waves.
 
• Later, Heinrich Hertz, a German physicist, applied Maxwell's theories to the production and reception of radio waves.
 
• Italian inventor Guglielmo Marconi after several years starting in 1894 built the first complete, commercially successful wireless telegraphy system based on airborne Hertzian waves or the radio waves in the year 1895.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Hopkinson’s test:__

 
 
• It is a full load test, used to test the efficiency of a DC machine.
 
• Temperature rise and commutation can be observed and maintained in the limit because this test is done under full load condition.
 
• It requires two identical machines that are coupled to each other. One of these two machines is operated as a generator to supply the mechanical power to the motor and the other is operated as a motor to drive the generator.
 
• It is also called a regenerative test or back to back test or heat run test.
 
 
 
• Guglielmo Marconi
 
 
• Italian physicist and inventor of the successful wireless telegraph (1896).
 
• He received the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1909.
 
• He worked on the development of shortwave wireless communication, which constitutes the basis of nearly all modern long-distance radio.
 
• It meant a giant leap – from an era of communication using wires to communicating without using wires. (Wireless).
 
 

 
• Michael Faraday:

 
 
• He is known as the Father of Electricity.
 
• He discovered the laws of electromagnetism.
 
• He also discovered the induction of electric current.
 
• He also discovered benzene in the year 1825.
 
• He also built the first electric generator and first electric motor.
